row.evidence: Process Street's pricing table marks 'SCIM user provisioning' and SAML SSO only on Enterprise (Contact sales), and its Okta SCIM guide says "This feature is only available in our Enterprise plan."
row.notes: Status unchanged (gated). Price change since June: the pricing page no longer lists any prices; Startup, Pro and Enterprise all show 'Contact sales' (June recorded Startup at $100/mo flat for 5 users and Pro from $15/u/mo), so team price fields are now null. SCIM and SAML SSO are Enterprise-only; SCIM is enabled by Process Street on request. Okta and Entra are set up with generic apps (Okta's SCIM 2.0 Test App, Entra non-gallery app) against https://public-api.process.st/api/scim with an API key as bearer token; Entra also provisions groups. The SSO article separately says JIT sign-in does not deprovision users. The public REST API (all plans, call quotas per plan) only lists users.

plans.name: Startup
plans.notes: Reduced-price Pro plan for businesses under 15 employees and $2M revenue; 50 API calls/month.

auth.token_source: Process Street API key generated by an Administrator on the organization's Integrations page

endpoints.notes: No SCIM endpoint reference is published; Users and Groups inferred from the Okta and Entra setup guides.

operations.notes: Okta guide enables Create Users, Update User Attributes and Deactivate Users; the HTTP verbs used for updates are not documented.

deprovision.notes: Docs say SCIM lets you 'add and remove users' but do not say whether Okta deactivate removes or suspends the member. Manual removal unassigns the user from groups, workflow runs, tasks and Pages (c33).

attributes.notes: Attribute names are the Okta mapping labels (Given name, Family name, Email, Primary email type, Display name, User type); exact SCIM paths are not published. Group attributes inferred from Entra group provisioning.

roles.how: Okta: 'User type' attribute (Admin, Member, Guest (Internal), Guest (External)), default Guest (Internal). Entra: app roles Admin, Builder, User, Guest assigned to users or groups, default User.

limitations.text: No gallery/OIN app: Okta uses the generic 'SCIM 2.0 Test App (OAuth Bearer Token)' and Entra a non-gallery 'Create your own application'.
Changing a user's email via SCIM needs a company domain that Process Street support sets up; passwords cannot be changed via SCIM.
SCIM must be enabled on the account by Process Street (Customer Success Manager or support).

auth.notes: Keys carry the permissions of the administrator who created them; no scopes.

capabilities.notes: The OpenAPI spec's Users tag has a single list operation; user lifecycle is only via SCIM.

endpoints.purpose: List all users (20 per page, cursor pagination)

webhooks_user_events.notes: Webhook triggers are task and workflow-run events only.

rate_limits.text: All requests are rate limited; 429 responses carry Retry-After. Plan quotas: Startup 50 API calls/month, Pro custom, Enterprise unlimited.

okta.notes: No OIN app (https://www.okta.com/integrations/process-street/ returns 404); vendor guide uses a custom SAML 2.0 app and Okta's generic SCIM 2.0 Test App.

entra.notes: No gallery app (Learn tutorial URL 404); vendor guide uses a non-gallery enterprise app.

onelogin.notes: OneLogin listed as a supported SAML SSO provider; provisioning not documented.

conflicts.text: The SSO article says Process Street 'does not support deprovisioning' (in the JIT/SSO context), while the Okta SCIM guide enables 'Deactivate Users' and the Entra guide says SCIM can 'add and remove users'.

open_questions: What SCIM deactivation does in Process Street (removal vs suspension), and whether it frees the seat or ends sessions, is not documented.
Whether SCIM requires SAML SSO to be configured first is ambiguous ('an SSO integration that supports SCIM provisioning').
SCIM filtering, pagination, PUT vs PATCH, discovery endpoints and rate limits are not documented.
Plan prices are no longer published; Startup and Pro per-user prices unknown.
Audit-log API availability is not documented.
